schema: CEH lab reels (one-off batch, scheduled 16-21 Nov 2026). Same fields as bank/reels.json, plus: term = terminal lines typed during that segment ('$ ' command, '! ' finding in yellow, '+ ' live/ok in green, '# ' comment in cyan, '> ' or plain = output). cta 'ceh' uses the CEH coming-soon call to action from config.json. Source: Nishant's CEH v13 Lab Hub artifact (narration scripts + rendered terminal demos); every target is his isolated practice lab or a purpose-built training target.

segments.say: Before you hack anything... build a lab. It's the only legal place to practice.
segments.show: Before you hack anything, build a lab. It's the only legal place to practice.

segments.say: VirtualBox, Kali Linux as the attacker, and Metasploitable two as the target... on a host-only network, so nothing escapes.
segments.show: VirtualBox, Kali Linux as the attacker and Metasploitable 2 as the target, on a host-only network so nothing escapes.

segments.say: First recon. A ping sweep finds the target.
segments.show: First recon: a ping sweep finds the target.

segments.say: Then a version scan. Every open port is a door... and an old version like vsftpd two point three point four is your first lead.
segments.show: Then a version scan. Every open port is a door, and an old version like vsftpd 2.3.4 is your first lead.

segments.say: The golden rule... only test systems you own, or are authorized to test.
segments.show: The golden rule: only test systems you own, or are authorized to test.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: Build your ethical hacking lab first (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: VirtualBox + Kali Linux + Metasploitable 2 on an isolated host-only network, then your first nmap ping sweep and version scan. Only test systems you own or are authorized to test.

reels.hook: This DNS mistake leaks the internal map

segments.say: One misconfigured D N S server can hand an attacker a map of your internal network.
segments.show: One misconfigured DNS server can hand an attacker a map of your internal network.

segments.say: Start passive. Dig shows the name servers and text records... and S P F often reveals which mail and cloud services a company uses.
segments.show: Start passive. dig shows the name servers and TXT records, and SPF often reveals which mail and cloud services a company uses.

segments.say: Now a zone transfer, against zonetransfer dot me... a domain built for this kind of training. The server dumps every record, including an internal host with a private I P.
segments.show: Now a zone transfer against zonetransfer.me, a domain built for this training. The server dumps every record, including an internal host with a private IP.

segments.say: theHarvester then collects emails and subdomains... phishing targets and new attack surface.
segments.show: theHarvester then collects emails and subdomains: phishing targets and new attack surface.

segments.say: The fix? Restrict zone transfers to trusted servers only.
segments.show: The fix: restrict zone transfers to trusted servers only.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: This DNS mistake leaks a company's internal map (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: Footprinting with dig and theHarvester, then a DNS zone transfer against zonetransfer.me, a domain built for training. A successful transfer leaks internal hostnames and IPs. Fix: restrict zone transfers to trusted servers.

reels.hook: Three nmap scans, open port to known flaw

segments.say: Three nmap scans in my lab... from what's open, to what's vulnerable.
segments.show: Three nmap scans in my lab: from what's open, to what's vulnerable.

segments.say: Dash capital S is a stealth SYN scan. Dash p dash checks all sixty five thousand ports.
segments.show: -sS is a stealth SYN scan. -p- checks all 65,535 ports.

segments.say: Dash s capital V gets the versions. Dash capital O fingerprints the operating system.
segments.show: -sV gets the versions. -O fingerprints the operating system.

segments.say: Then the vuln scripts. Nmap flags the vsftpd backdoor... and names the C V E.
segments.show: Then the vuln scripts. nmap flags the vsftpd backdoor and names the CVE.

segments.say: Exam tip... a SYN scan is half-open. It never completes the handshake, which is why it's quieter.
segments.show: Exam tip: a SYN scan is half-open. It never completes the handshake, which is why it's quieter.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: 3 nmap scans: from open port to known flaw (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: A SYN scan of all ports, a version and OS scan, then NSE vuln scripts that flag the vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor (CVE-2011-2523), all against a practice target in an isolated lab.

reels.hook: This server lists its users to strangers

segments.say: Scanning finds the doors. Enumeration asks each one... who are you?
segments.show: Scanning finds the doors. Enumeration asks each one: who are you?

segments.say: Enum four linux pulls the user accounts... and every username feeds the password attacks that come next.
segments.show: enum4linux pulls the user accounts, and every username feeds the password attacks that come next.

segments.say: Smbclient, with no password, lists the shares. That anonymous null session is a leak all by itself.
segments.show: smbclient with no password lists the shares. That anonymous null session is a leak all by itself.

segments.say: And S N M P still answers to the default community string... public.
segments.show: And SNMP still answers to the default community string: public.

segments.say: The fix... disable null sessions, and change default S N M P strings.
segments.show: The fix: disable null sessions, and change default SNMP strings.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: This server lists its users to strangers (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: Enumeration in an isolated lab: enum4linux finds user accounts, an SMB null session lists shares, and SNMP answers to the default 'public' string. Fix: disable null sessions and change SNMP defaults.

reels.hook: How a version number becomes a critical risk

segments.say: An old version number looks harmless... until you map it to a known exploit.
segments.show: An old version number looks harmless, until you map it to a known exploit.

segments.say: Nikto scans the web server... an outdated Apache, a phpinfo page leaking config, an exposed admin tool.
segments.show: Nikto scans the web server: an outdated Apache, a phpinfo page leaking config, an exposed admin tool.

segments.say: Searchsploit maps vsftpd two point three point four to a documented backdoor.
segments.show: searchsploit maps vsftpd 2.3.4 to a documented backdoor.
term: # a version becomes a named risk

segments.say: Scanners like Nessus or OpenVAS score it with C V S S. The backdoor is a critical ten... so it gets fixed first.
segments.show: Scanners like Nessus or OpenVAS score it with CVSS. The backdoor is a critical 10, so it gets fixed first.

segments.say: Prioritize by C V S S, patch... then re-scan to prove it's fixed.
segments.show: Prioritize by CVSS, patch, then re-scan to prove it's fixed.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: How a version number becomes a critical risk (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: Nikto flags an outdated web server, searchsploit maps vsftpd 2.3.4 to a known backdoor, and a CVSS-scored scan rates it critical 10.0. Prioritise by CVSS, patch, then re-scan.

reels.topic: System hacking: passwords and privilege escalation

segments.say: In my lab, a weak password falls almost instantly. Here's how... and how to stop it.
segments.show: In my lab, a weak password falls almost instantly. Here's how, and how to stop it.

segments.say: Hydra guesses passwords against the live S S H service. That's an online attack.
segments.show: Hydra guesses passwords against the live SSH service. That's an online attack.

segments.say: John the Ripper cracks stolen hashes offline... where no lockout can slow it down.
segments.show: John the Ripper cracks stolen hashes offline, where no lockout can slow it down.

segments.say: Then privilege escalation. Find the S U I D binaries... a misconfigured one can lead to root.
segments.show: Then privilege escalation. Find the SUID binaries: a misconfigured one can lead to root.
term: # SUID nmap can enable privilege escalation

segments.say: Defend it with account lockout and M F A, strong salted hashing, and least privilege.
segments.show: Defend it with account lockout and MFA, strong salted hashing, and least privilege.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: This password fell in seconds (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: Online guessing with Hydra, offline hash cracking with John the Ripper, and a SUID privilege-escalation check, all on a practice VM in an isolated lab. Defences: lockout + MFA, strong salted hashing, least privilege.

reels.topic: Malware analysis from the defender's side
reels.hook: Check a malware file without running it

segments.say: A suspicious file lands on your desk. Here's how a defender checks it... safely, in a sandbox.
segments.show: A suspicious file lands on your desk. Here's how a defender checks it, safely, in a sandbox.

segments.say: Hash it, and check that hash against threat intel like VirusTotal.
segments.show: Hash it, and check that hash against threat intel like VirusTotal.
term: # check the hash against threat intel

segments.say: Strings reveals a hard-coded U R L and a suspicious command... a trojan phoning home.
segments.show: strings reveals a hard-coded URL and a suspicious command: a trojan phoning home.

segments.say: A signature scan confirms it's known-bad. And netstat shows an unexpected outbound connection.
segments.show: A signature scan confirms it's known-bad. And netstat shows an unexpected outbound connection.

segments.say: Exam tip... static analysis reads a file without running it. Dynamic analysis runs it in a sandbox.
segments.show: Exam tip: static analysis reads a file without running it. Dynamic analysis runs it in a sandbox.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: Check a malware file without running it (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: Defender's view in a sandbox: hash the file, read its strings for a hard-coded C2 URL, scan it with a signature engine, and spot the unexpected outbound connection. Static vs dynamic analysis is an exam favourite.

reels.hook: Why FTP passwords are visible to anyone

segments.say: On my own lab segment, here's what a man-in-the-middle actually sees.
segments.show: On my own lab segment, here's what a man-in-the-middle actually sees.

segments.say: Ettercap poisons A R P... so traffic between the target and the gateway flows through us.
segments.show: Ettercap poisons ARP, so traffic between the target and the gateway flows through us.
term: # we now sit in the middle

segments.say: Tcpdump on port twenty one. The F T P login appears... username and password, in plain text.
segments.show: tcpdump on port 21. The FTP login appears: username and password, in plain text.

segments.say: The fix is encryption. S F T P, S S H, H T T P S... plus switch port security and dynamic A R P inspection.
segments.show: The fix is encryption: SFTP, SSH, HTTPS, plus switch port security and dynamic ARP inspection.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: Why FTP passwords are visible to anyone (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: ARP poisoning with Ettercap on an isolated lab segment, then tcpdump shows an FTP login in cleartext. Fix: SFTP/SSH/HTTPS, switch port security and dynamic ARP inspection.

reels.hook: One quote mark broke the login

segments.say: On a deliberately vulnerable app in my lab, one quote mark can break a login.
segments.show: On a deliberately vulnerable app in my lab, one quote mark can break a login.

segments.say: Gobuster finds the hidden paths first... an admin panel, a database tool.
segments.show: Gobuster finds the hidden paths first: an admin panel, a database tool.

segments.say: Then the classic test... quote, OR one equals one. The query is always true, so the login is bypassed.
segments.show: Then the classic test: ' OR '1'='1. The query is always true, so the login is bypassed.

segments.say: Sqlmap confirms it, and lists the databases.
segments.show: sqlmap confirms it, and lists the databases.

segments.say: The real fix is parameterized queries... so input can never change the query.
segments.show: The real fix is parameterized queries, so input can never change the query.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: One quote mark broke the login (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: On DVWA in an isolated lab: gobuster finds hidden paths, a ' OR '1'='1 test bypasses the login, and sqlmap confirms the injection. The definitive fix is parameterized queries.

segments.say: Only ever test an access point you own. Mine is called LAB TEST A P.
segments.show: Only ever test an access point you own. Mine is called LAB-TEST-AP.

segments.say: Airmon puts the card in monitor mode. Airodump lists nearby networks... B S S I D, channel, encryption.
segments.show: airmon-ng puts the card in monitor mode. airodump-ng lists nearby networks: BSSID, channel, encryption.

segments.say: Capture the four-way handshake... then crack it offline. A weak passphrase falls in seconds.
segments.show: Capture the four-way handshake, then crack it offline. A weak passphrase falls in seconds.

segments.say: The fix... a long random passphrase, W P A three, or enterprise eight-oh-two-dot-one-X.
segments.show: The fix: a long random passphrase, WPA3, or enterprise 802.1X.

segments.say: Follow for more C E H labs.
segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: Weak Wi-Fi password, cracked offline (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: On my own test access point: monitor mode, capture the WPA2 handshake, then crack a weak passphrase offline. Fix: a long random passphrase, WPA3 or enterprise 802.1X.

reels.topic: Mobile app secrets and exposed OT
reels.hook: API keys hiding inside an app

segments.say: Developers sometimes hard-code secrets into mobile apps. Here's how to find them... in an app you own.
segments.show: Developers sometimes hard-code secrets into mobile apps. Here's how to find them, in an app you own.

segments.say: A D B connects to the Android emulator. Apktool unpacks the A P K.
segments.show: ADB connects to the Android emulator. apktool unpacks the APK.

segments.say: One grep... and there's an A P I key, hard-coded in the app.
segments.show: One grep, and there's an API key, hard-coded in the app.
term: # anyone who downloads the app can extract it

segments.say: And on the industrial side, nmap finds Modbus on port five zero two... a lab P L C with no authentication.
segments.show: And on the industrial side, nmap finds Modbus on port 502: a lab PLC with no authentication.

segments.say: No secrets in apps... and keep O T networks segmented from everything else.
segments.show: No secrets in apps, and keep OT networks segmented from everything else.

segments.show: Follow for more CEH labs.

post.title: API keys hiding inside an app (CEH lab) #Shorts
post.caption: Unpack your own Android app with apktool and grep finds a hard-coded API key; nmap finds Modbus with no auth on a lab PLC simulator. Fix: no secrets in apps, segment OT networks.

segments.say: The number one cloud risk isn't an exploit. It's misconfiguration.
segments.show: The number one cloud risk isn't an exploit. It's misconfiguration.

segments.say: My own test bucket, listed with no credentials at all... a database dump, and an employee file.
segments.show: My own test bucket, listed with no credentials at all: a database dump and an employee file.
